sample: Fictional company, people and figures, for demonstration. Every value below is stated by this file; nothing in the outputs goes beyond it.
description: Order orchestration for buy-online-pickup-in-store and marketplace orders

drivers.statement: Offer same-day buy-online-pickup-in-store in every store
Take marketplace partner orders through one governed API
SAP S/4 stays the system of record for inventory
Apigee X is the enterprise API standard
Order volume peaks at three times normal from November to December

actors.name: Store associate
actors.description: Picks, stages and hands over pickup orders

actors.name: Marketplace partner
actors.description: Submits orders and reads their status by API

external_systems.name: Warehouse management
external_systems.description: Pick and stage tasks in stores

nfrs.requirement: PCI scope excluded from Order Hub

decisions.title: Event backbone for order events
decisions.context: Pick queues must be rebuilt from order events after a warehouse system outage; events must be replayable for 7 days (CTO statement 2026-09-02).
decisions.rationale: Only option that meets the 7-day replay requirement natively, with per-key ordering for order lifecycles.
consequences: The platform team operates a managed Kafka cluster with a schema registry

decisions.title: Order store database
decisions.context: Order state changes must be transactional across order lines and fulfilment steps.
decisions.rationale: Meets transactional needs at the stated peak with the skills the team already has.
consequences: Read replicas serve status queries at peak
Partitioning by order month is planned before wave 2

decisions.title: API entry point for stores and partners
decisions.context: Marketplace partners and store systems need one governed, rate-limited entry point.
decisions.rationale: The enterprise API standard; partner keys, quotas and threat protection come with it.
consequences: One extra network hop on every call; measured against the p95 target once it is set

risks.risk: Warehouse connector throughput falls short of peak pick volume
risks.mitigation: Load test the connector at three times normal volume before the wave 2 exit

risks.risk: Nightly SAP inventory file makes intraday promises inaccurate
risks.mitigation: Decide on near-real-time inventory events before wave 3 (new ADR)

risks.risk: Payment data enters Order Hub and widens PCI scope
risks.mitigation: Payment tokens stay with the payment provider; a contract test rejects card fields

risks.risk: Store POS upgrade dates are not known

waves.goal: Orders are created and stored through the API gateway
waves.entry: Gateway and Order service in staging; availability probe live
waves.exit: Associates in 20 pilot stores create and read orders for two weeks without a severity-1 incident
waves.rollback: Route pilot stores back to the legacy order screen

waves.entry: Wave 1 exit met; warehouse connector load-tested
waves.exit: Pick requests reach the warehouse system for every store; nightly inventory reconciles
waves.rollback: Pause the warehouse connector; picks continue through the legacy batch

security.control: Store associates sign in with Northwind SSO (OIDC) at the gateway; partners use API keys with quotas
TLS 1.2 or later on every integration; mutual TLS between gateway and Order service

deployment.caption: Where each container runs. Google Cloud for Order Hub; SAP and warehouse systems stay in the Northwind data centre.
